title: A part retired while on order can still be received and picked
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919), a role that has 'Part Library & Inventory → View', 'Create & Edit' and 'Delete'.
  • Vendor {Vendor-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST PL ONORDER Vendor) exists.
  • Inventory part {Part-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-ONORDER-01), vendor {Vendor-A}, is tracked at {Location-A} with 0 in its default bin.
  • Work order {Work-order-1} (for example S2-15440) is open and its approved line {Line-1} (for example "ZZAUTOTEST PL ONORDER line") has two requests for {Part-A} from {Vendor-A}: {Request-A} is already ordered on purchase order {Purchase-order-A} (for example PO-1234), and {Request-B} is not yet ordered.
  • {Part-A} was set inactive after that.
custom_steps:
1. On {Work-order-1}'s Parts tab order {Request-B} with its "Order" action.
  2. Open {Purchase-order-A}, click "Receive", type an invoice number (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-ONORDER-INV), delivered quantity 1, Cost 10.00 and Sell 20.00, and click "Receive".
  3. Back on {Work-order-1}'s Parts tab, pick the received {Part-A}.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: {Request-B} is ordered (it shows on a purchase order); no inactive-part refusal appears.
  • Step 2: The delivery is received with {Part-A}.
  • Step 3: {Part-A} is picked onto {Work-order-1} (status "Picked").

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10647; story SV-10822 (Story 9, Inactive Parts Cannot Be Added to New Work); PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, v29 (14 Oct 2026 copy), S9-E6, read 14 Oct 2026; design canvas 13 Oct copy: no board shows this. Tech plan "Parts Lifecycle Update — Technical Implementation Plan", 7 Oct 2026 (informs, never overrules), §5 Modified endpoints. Source-verified 14 October 2026; not yet build-verified (no Part Lifecycle QA build exists).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S9-E6: “A part that becomes inactive while it is on an open purchase order or a special order can still be received, and picked onto the work order that ordered it. Ordering an existing part request is not new work.”
  • Tech plan (Parts Lifecycle Update, 7 Oct 2026), §5 Modified endpoints: “Not refused: re-saving the same part (S9-E2), ordering an existing part request (S9-E6), pick, receive, split, invoice”
